statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low) with no Nasdaq-100 price path observable inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress of 67% (high) while the Strait of Hormuz stays shut after more than seven months, Washington has rejected Tehran's seven-day reopening plan, and four vessel strikes were reported in the strait between 1 and 4 October.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, 00:00-02:00 Berlin on 5 October, where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on weekend-gap and thin-liquidity discontinuity risk rather than on observed structure.
headline: Hormuz stays shut after Washington's rejection while Tail holds its halt-session floor, with CME futures closed until 22:00Z
body: CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor of 3%. The last observed structure was orderly and two-way: the cash index set a record intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, surrendered it in full, and closed at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00% from a 30,501.60 previous close, in the lower half of its 30,737.07-31,017.53 range. September NQ futures settled at 31,049, up 0.94%, which is the reference for any weekend gap. A record close that gives back its own high is mean-reversion-friendly rather than evidence of a persistent one-way path, which is why Tail is held at the floor even as the geopolitical backdrop stays unresolved. Stress is high at 67%, a point firmer than the previous hour. The Strait of Hormuz has now been largely blocked or disrupted for more than seven months and remains closed to normal commercial transit. Parliament speaker and lead negotiator Qalibaf said on Sunday that "the era of wasting time and dictating unilateral demands is over" and that the strait "will not open until our seven conditions based on the Islamabad memorandum are met". Foreign minister Araghchi said Iran is serious about diplomacy and, if attacked, is more prepared than before; foreign ministry spokesman Baghaei said Washington remains focused on the nuclear file while reopening the strait is Tehran's main goal. Against that, President Trump rejected the seven-day reopening proposal last week, said on Saturday that Iran faces a choice between the easy way and the hard way, and indicated that military action could resume after the 3 November midterms. The United States has announced a third carrier strike group and roughly 9,000 additional troops for the region, alongside two Patriot batteries deployed in recent weeks, and four vessel strikes were reported in the strait between 1 and 4 October, all on the Omani side, each by an unidentified projectile. Both the military and negotiation tracks are therefore live and unresolved, which under this contract is a Stress and Confidence matter rather than a Tail one: Tail measures the pathological price path, not the importance of the backdrop. The pricing of that backdrop is notably calm. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59%, WTI fell about 1.9% to roughly $91 as the G7 prepared to deploy 100 million barrels of reserves over four months under IEA oversight, and Middle Eastern crude exports have recovered to near pre-conflict levels. The macro backdrop is softer but not easier. September payrolls came in at +29,000 against +90,000 expected with unemployment at 4.2%, yet Treasury yields reversed higher into Friday's close, the 2-year at 4.8414% and the 10-year at 5.2939%, and October hike probabilities settled near 15-16%. The Federal Reserve's latest published H.15 release puts the 1 October 2-year at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%. An elevated long end alongside a weakening labour market is a persistent stressor, not an observed path risk. Confidence is high at 88%: Friday's closing levels and ranges, the futures settlement, yields, oil, VIX, the Sunday geopolitical record and the full week-ahead calendar with consensus figures are all verified. The one genuine gap is the absence of any live price path during the weekend halt. The shared Finviz context file was not usable this run, carrying a collection timestamp of 29 September and a partial collection status, so this assessment rests entirely on independent research. The danger window is deliberately narrow and covers the 22:00Z reopen and the hour after it, where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on weekend-gap and thin-liquidity discontinuity risk. It decays from 00:00Z on the base case that reopening discovery is orderly and two-way, and would have to be revised upward instead if price were observed holding a session extreme with shallow pullbacks or extending repeatedly after failed retracements.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Claude held Tail at 3% in every slot, with every hour mapping to EA_ON and green and the dominant mode normal throughout, reflecting a market that was either in orderly two-way trade or closed. Stress climbed from 60% at 18:00Z on 3 October to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October as the weekend geopolitical checkpoints opened, then eased through 73%, 70%, 68%, 66% and a 64% low at 14:00Z as those checkpoints resolved into stated positions, before settling at 66-67% in the final hours once the Sunday statements and the latest strait incident were verified. Confidence stayed in a tight 83-88% band and finished the window at its high.
outlookSummary: The remaining closed Sunday hours carry no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure, so Tail is held between 3% and 4% through 20:00Z while Stress stays near 67% on the closed strait and the rejected reopening proposal. Tail then steps to 9% in the final closed hour and is raised to 22% and 20%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, which the published danger window covers. From 00:00Z it decays to 14%, 11% and single digits through the Asian and European sessions on the base case that reopening discovery is orderly and two-way, with Stress easing from 69% at the reopen to a 58% low late in the European morning. Tail lifts again to 11%, 15% and a 16% session peak around Monday's 13:30Z cash open, the 13:45Z final S&P Global Services PMI and the 14:00Z ISM Services PMI, all treated as checkpoints rather than automatic blocks, then eases to 14%, 12% and 11% on the assumption the print is absorbed with a normal retracement. No published forecast hour reaches the block threshold.
